text:
jen: heads up — CI in infra repo started failing repeatedly on the gpu-canary pipeline this morning. failing step: helm upgrade (times out) + cache restore 403 in some matrix lanes.

sam: seen it. which job in the matrix? region or instance type?

jen: matrix is region x nodepool-type (gcp-us-west1/spot-gpu-small etc). failures are mostly in asia nodes and one us-west spot lane. logs: 
```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: timed out waiting for the condition
NAME: gpu-canary
LAST DEPLOYED: Tue Mar 12 09:10:22 2025
REVISION: 3
STATUS: pending-upgrade
NOTES: 
  1. Run `kubectl --context=canary get pods` to see status
```

kai: hmm that helm message usually means the deployment never reached Ready. could be node scheduling or image pull. any kube events attached?

ana: (typo: ana) i saw ImagePullBackOff on one of the asia lanes a few hours ago — registry 429 spikes. but the helm timeout only started after we added the new autoscaler rules.

sam: also noticed the GH Actions runner restore-cache step returned 403 for a couple lanes: `actions/cache` returned 403 from storage.googleapis.com. we rotated the service account last week — maybe creds not propagated.

jen: exact cache error snippet: 
```
Restore cache failed: Server returned 403.
Request-Id: xxxxx
```

jen: The combination is causing the pipeline to take longer and then helm times out. The matrix is configured with concurrency group per-region which means these timeouts cascade.

kai: is concurrency: group: infra-${{ matrix.region }} ? if so, a hung job blocks others in the same region. we should limit concurrency or split the matrix.

sam: agreed. temporary mitigation: reduce helm timeout and skip cache-restore for non-critical lanes. also we can set `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: false` to avoid cancels if they pile up.

ana: workaround for cache 403 — re-create the storage token pair or set `cache: key: ${{ runner.os }}-infra-${{ matrix.region }}-${{ matrix.nodepool }}` so it uses different keys while we debug.

jen: another thing: terraform apply is occasionally hitting state lock errors after a failed helm step: `Error locking state: Resource is in use by another operation`. People have been doing manual force-unlock which is scary.

kai: recommend adding `retry` wrapper for terraform apply in the GH action with exponential backoff and a small window to wait for lock cleanup. also enforce single apply per region using `concurrency` at the workflow level only for terraform jobs.

sam: ops note — runners on spot instances in asia are getting preempted frequently; that aligns with the matrix lanes failing there. we should move gpu-canary tests to a dedicated non-spot runner pool for now.

devops-bot: deploy-bot detected multiple failing jobs in workflow infra/gpu-provision (5 failures in last 30m). Notifying owners.

ana: TL;DR action items:
- rotate/validate cache SA creds (ana + infra)
- temporarily reduce matrix concurrency for canary flows (sam)
- add retry + force-unlock safety for terraform (kai)
- run gpu-canary on dedicated non-spot runners until preemption window ends (infra team)
- increase helm timeout only if needed after addressing scheduling/errors (jen)

sam: I'll open a quick PR to change workflow concurrency and skip cache restore for non-critical matrix lanes. tagging @ana for creds.

jen: thanks — will follow up if helm timeouts persist after these changes. :thumbsup:
